title: Dynamic Pseudogap Model: Analytic Results vs Monte Carlo Numerics
abstract: Recently proposed dynamic pseudogap model analytical results for spectral density of an electron scattered by random time-dependent Gaussian field representing fluctuations with finite nesting vector ${\bf Q}$, characteristic oscillation frequency $ω_0$ and damping $γ$, leading to pseudogap formation, are compared with exact numerical solution by Monte Carlo (MC) approach. We consider both commensurate (real) and incommensurate (complex) fluctuations, for a wide range of parameters of the model. Electron Green's function is approximated either by a double Poisson series with history-dependent Bogoliubov gaps or by exact static continued fraction solution. In the coherent regime double-series representation provides description of dynamic sideband formation in the spectral density. As coherence is progressively lost, the theory crosses over to the quasistatic fluctuating-gap regime described by the exact continued-fraction solution. The exact MC solution overcomes the limitations of analytic approach, such as neglect of Magnus-type corrections in commuting approximation, and establish the limits of analytic approach, as well as confirming the exactness of continued fraction solution in static limit. In general, analytic expressions demonstrate rather satisfactory agreement with exact MC numerics within their limits, confirming the overall qualitative physical picture of dynamic pseudogap formation.
summary: This work rigorously compares analytic predictions for the spectral density in a dynamic pseudogap model against exact Monte Carlo simulations. By analyzing different fluctuation regimes, the authors map out the precise limits of validity for various theoretical approximations. The findings confirm the physical picture of pseudogap formation while establishing the necessary conditions for the reliability of analytical methods.
main_problem: The paper compares analytic theoretical results for the spectral density of an electron in a dynamic pseudogap model against exact Monte Carlo (MC) numerical solutions.
main_result: Analytic expressions show satisfactory agreement with MC numerics within their respective limits, confirming the qualitative picture of dynamic pseudogap formation, though the MC approach reveals limitations in the analytic approximations.
method: The study employs both analytical techniques (double Poisson series, continued fraction) and numerical simulations (Monte Carlo) to calculate the electron Green's function and spectral density.
model_or_system: The model describes an electron scattered by random time-dependent Gaussian fluctuations (representing charge or spin density waves) characterized by a nesting vector Q, oscillation frequency $\omega_0$, and damping $\gamma$.
key_observables: Spectral density $A(\omega)$, Density of States (DOS), and the main quasiparticle-like peak parameters (position, height, FWHM).
important_parameters: Fluctuation parameters ($\omega_0, \gamma$), momentum/spatial parameter ($\xi$), and the coherence rate $\Gamma_{	ext{eff}}$.
main_assumptions: The analytic approach relies on approximations like neglecting Magnus-type corrections and assuming specific regimes (coherent vs. quasistatic).
figures_summary: Figures compare the spectral density and DOS from the series expansion against MC results across various parameter regimes, highlighting points of agreement and divergence.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the results from the double Poisson series (coherent regime) and the continued fraction solution (quasistatic limit) against the benchmark MC solution, analyzing the crossover region and identifying the parameter space where each method is valid.
why_interesting: The rigorous comparison between analytical approximations and exact numerical solutions in a strongly fluctuating, disordered environment provides crucial insight into the breakdown points of standard theoretical tools for correlated electron systems.
